long_biography.plain_text:
Seeing contemporary African paintings and sculptures in Paris changed Jean Pigozzi’s collecting direction. After visiting Magiciens de la Terre in 1989, he hired curator André Magnin to seek out artists across sub-Saharan Africa. Magnin travelled and maintained the relationships; Pigozzi chose which artists to collect in depth. Their team also supplied paints and canvases where suitable materials were difficult to obtain.

His support for research took a different form in Panama. On land he owned, he built the Liquid Jungle Lab, giving visiting scientists access to tropical forest and coastal waters. Researchers from Woods Hole, the Smithsonian and Madrid’s Royal Botanical Garden advised on its design and operation, creating facilities for studies of plankton, coral, mangroves and coastal currents.
